authority: Experiment-only authored navigation from inspected source, not an execution trace, verified requirement, or claim that tests passed.

given: An admin has submitted a supported JSON-export ZIP containing shared attachments, and the import creation request is accepted.
when: The import's queued bootstrap and page tasks run, followed by the conditional processed-event persistence pass.
then: Shared JSON attachments are finalized before the Import becomes Processed.
Successful persistence moves the Import from Processed to Completed; Processed still displays Processing.
A persistence failure may be retried and may eventually mark the Import Errored; failing to remove the source archive after Completed does not roll back completion.

intendedChecks.declaration: imports collections, documents and attachments from the fixture
intendedChecks.limit: The helper seeds a task, drives task.perform with queue scheduling mocked, and calls the processed handler directly; not an uploaded ZIP through the live queue and UI.

intendedChecks.declaration: completes the import when source archive cleanup fails
intendedChecks.limit: Checks persisted Completed despite failed source-attachment deletion, not the displayed list.
Its inspected case uses Notion, not the JSON archive branch.

gaps: No live queue attempts or emitted-event delivery is proven by these links.
The client list refresh/update path after backend state changes is not modeled.
The listed test declarations are intended checks, not a complete test catalog or proof of passing tests.

checkpoints.fact: The client uploads the ZIP as a workspace-import attachment, then consumes imports.create; a successful create response is not proof the background import finished.
The route authorizes JSON import creation and archive access and creates a Created Import with the archive storage key in scratch.
JSON bootstrap reads the archive and prepares page tasks and an attachment manifest.
Per-page task processing saves task output and schedules the next task; this does not itself mean the Import is Completed.
A completed task looks for another Created task; if none remains, it runs the JSON finalization hook before marking the Import Processed.
The JSON hook creates shared attachment rows and blobs from the archive manifest before the Processed state transition; a non-duplicate failure can interrupt this handoff.
The task handoff saves Processed and emits the processed transition; that state still renders Processing, not Completed.

The imports.processed handler uses attachment rows when rewriting persisted content, creates collections and documents, and saves Completed. A failure stores an error and rethrows for retry; exhausted failure can mark Errored.
After a persistence exception, the processor records an error and rethrows; a retry may revisit the processed handler if eligible.
When the processor's failure handling runs, it can mark the Import Errored; Errored displays Failed.
After Completed persists, the processor attempts to remove the source archive. Failure to remove it is logged without reverting Completed.
The list maps Created, InProgress, and Processed to Processing; Completed to Completed; Errored to Failed. The client refresh/update path that supplies this row is not mapped here.

progression: t01: upload -> accept [operation-handoff] when imports.create request is accepted
t02: accept -> bootstrap [creation-event] when imports.create event is processed and bootstrap is scheduled
t03: bootstrap -> page-tasks [task-wave] when bootstrap prepares page tasks
t03b: page-tasks -> task-handoff [task-completed] when a page task completes and completion handoff runs
t04: task-handoff -> page-tasks [next-task] when a further Created page task exists; repeat page processing
t05: task-handoff -> finalize-attachments [final-task] when no Created task remains
t06: finalize-attachments -> processed [state-change] when JSON attachment finalization succeeds
t07: processed -> display [observation] when the list receives Processed before completion; it still says Processing
t08: processed -> persist [event-handoff] when imports.processed is delivered and persistence begins
t09: persist -> retry [failure] when persistence throws and the processor records an error and rethrows
t10: retry -> persist [retry] when the processed event receives another eligible attempt
t11: retry -> errored [exhaustion] when failure handling runs after attempts are exhausted
t12: persist -> cleanup [success] when collections and documents are saved and Completed persists
t13: cleanup -> display [post-completion] when archive removal succeeds or its failure is logged; Completed remains saved
t14: errored -> display [failure-display] when the list receives Errored; it displays Failed
